issues.legal_issue: A purchaser is entitled to recover earnest money when an acquisition already notified before the sale agreement is later completed, making the agreement impossible to perform, and the contract provides for return of the earnest money upon acquisition.
material_facts: The purchaser and landowner entered into an agreement for the sale of a share of land after a preliminary acquisition notification had been published.
The landowner had not disclosed the notification to the purchaser.
The agreement required the landowner to return the earnest money without interest if the government acquired the land.
A later declaration confirmed the public purpose and the land was acquired.
The purchaser sued for return of the earnest money, but the first appellate court dismissed the suit on the ground that the purchaser was not ready and willing to perform.
The Supreme Court considered an appeal from the dismissal of the purchaser’s claim for refund.
issues.conclusion: The agreement was frustrated when the acquisition was confirmed, and the purchaser was entitled under the contractual term and Section 33 of the Contract Act to recover the earnest money. Readiness and willingness to perform were irrelevant once the acquisition notification prevented a valid conveyance. The trial court’s decree for refund was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, publication of a preliminary notification restricts the owner from dealing with the land as a free agent; a later sale or encumbrance does not bind the government. A declaration under Section 6 conclusively establishes the public purpose for the acquisition. Under Section 33 of the Contract Act, a contingent contract becomes enforceable when the event making performance impossible occurs. Where the contract also requires return of earnest money upon acquisition, the purchaser may enforce that term; readiness and willingness to perform do not affect the entitlement once performance has become futile. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: appeal_from_denial_of_earnest_money_refund and land_sale_agreement and acquisition_notification_preceded_agreement and acquisition_was_confirmed and contract_requires_refund_on_acquisition

predicates.appeal_from_denial_of_earnest_money_refu: The proceeding is an appeal from a decision denying a purchaser’s claim to recover earnest money.
predicates.land_sale_agreement: A purchaser and landowner entered into an agreement for the sale of land.
predicates.acquisition_notification_preceded_agreem: An official notification proposing acquisition of the land was published before the sale agreement was made.
predicates.acquisition_was_confirmed: A later official declaration confirmed the acquisition purpose and the land was acquired.
predicates.contract_requires_refund_on_acquisition: The agreement requires the landowner to return the earnest money if the government acquires the land.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges denial of an earnest-money refund under a land sale agreement, and an acquisition notification preceded the agreement, the acquisition was later confirmed, and the contract requires a refund upon acquisition, the purchaser is entitled to recover the earnest money.
